MIDI and uncompressed score-partwise MusicXML import append ordinary tracker patterns and instruments, then select the imported song order. Existing SFX patterns remain in place. Generic imports quantize notes to sixteenth-note rows; explicit Forge score profiles preserve their declared channel and row timing; one song tempo is retained; excess polyphony beyond three tonal voices plus one noise voice is rejected. Compressed MXL, score transcription, tablature, alternate audio models and automatic Audio Runtime enablement are not included.

Audio interchange and workshop

In AUDIO, open Audio workshop examples to add editable notes while retaining old patterns and SFX; the song order is replaced and Undo restores it. Export MIDI and Export MusicXML create supported score conversions through Save As. Read the warnings: instrument envelopes, duty, SFX bindings and gameplay are not full score backups. Reimport retains supported note timing, channels, cuts and volume. Larger destination patterns may add reported silent padding. Native JSON/ZIP remains the complete project backup. Listening and external-software acceptance remain separate.

Native graphics recovery

General ROM Analysis inspects unknown engines independently of the emulator. In Raw CHR patterns, Preview native tile import then Import as new tile sheet adds editable physical CHR-ROM tiles with saved source SHA-256/range evidence. The generated grayscale sheet is excluded from builds by default; its palette/layout do not recover original maps. Download active sheet CHR exports edited bitplanes. CHR RAM, compressed graphics, native maps, collision and Audio need other supported methods; generic inspection is not universal recovery.

Checkpoints and reversible experiments

For a ROM loaded in EMULATOR, RE runtime tools can save bounded full-machine Checkpoints, run explicit controller-input scripts and apply reversible RAM byte edits. Restoring rewinds CPU/PPU/APU/video state and clears stale observations. Reset or ROM replacement clears session checkpoints. Active experiment rollback checkpoints cannot be deleted. Scripts replay inputs; they do not discover stages, health or enemy semantics. I/O and ROM/mapper register patches are rejected.

Source workspace

CODE → Open source workspace retains original multi-file sources separately from the active project. The declared Forge-6502 NROM profile resolves literal .include/.incbin paths, builds an independent ROM and exports source ZIP/JSON, expanded ASM and source/symbol maps. Save this workspace before closing. Building does not replace the project or emulator, or merge generated gameplay/audio. NESmaker/foreign dialect translation, Lua execution, general linking and mapper profiles remain unimplemented.

Assembly

CODE retains official 6502 assembly, labels, macros and segmented .org output. Audio Runtime is available only in generated code paths; enable authored custom assembly or Audio Runtime, not both. Disassembly inspects the mapped CPU window; it is not a recovered source project.

Scenes, collision and animation RE

RE → Open spatial RE workbench reads native tables from four exact investigated ROM revisions. Mega Man 2 exposes stage-dependent collision and raw screen slots; Ninja Gaiden exposes rooms, native ground kinds and 13 player action scripts; Zelda II exposes overworld terrain; Castlevania II exposes layouts and raw tile categories before conditional block substitution. Select a cell for its source byte, inspect native animation durations/pieces, and export selected evidence. Colors and animation grayscale palettes are illustrative. These reports do not import playable scenes, native physics or complete behavior; Zelda side-view collision and non-Ninja animation decoders remain unsupported. Unknown revisions use the existing runtime tools. See SPATIAL_RE.md in the review kit for controls, evidence and limits.
